title: USB VIP device-mode integration gotchas -- USB2.0 HS/FS/LS serial-interface FAQ digest (VIP=Host, DUT=Device)
summary: Digest of FAQ.txt Sec 2 (USB 2.0, lines 1031-1252) plus related items, filtered for relevance to THIS project's confirmed topology: VIP runs Host, DUT is Device (udc_DWC_usb31_params.svh MODE=0, GCTL.PrtCapDir=Device), matching UVM/HDL user guide topology Sec 5.4 'USB VIP Host and DUT Device' (serial interface, no PIPE3). CLOCKING (hard requirement, all roles): VIP's serial interface needs a 4x-oversampled input clock because clock recovery is always enabled. USB2.0 HS/FS/LS: 1.92 GT/s (4x 480 MT/s) on usb_20_serial_if.clk (FAQ line 1140-1141; GS guide lines 296-297 restate it). SS: 20 GT/s (4x 5 GT/s) on usb_ss_serial_if.ssclk. GS guide Sec 2.1.1 (lines 242-276) gives a full 8-phase clock-gen 'initial'/'forever' block usable as a template for the 2.0 clock at its own period. PROTOCOL: Host VIP's SOF generation is OFF by default (FAQ 2.1.1, line 1037) -- must be explicitly driven via svt_usb_protocol_service SOF Command over a service channel; check this first if the Device DUT expects periodic SOF/keep-alive and none appears. LINK-LAYER TIMERS (svt_usb_configuration real attributes): utmi_reset_duration (default SVT_USB_20_HS_FS_8_BIT_INTERFACE_UTMI_CLOCK_PERIOD*10, FAQ 2.2.4); poweron_auto_attach_delay (default 0=starts attached; >0=starts detached+auto-attaches after delay; <0=starts detached, needs manual ATTACH_DEVICE physical-service command, FAQ 2.2.5); Tdrsmdn = host downstream resume duration, default SVT_USB_TDRSMDN_MIN (FAQ 2.3.4); Tdrsmup = device upstream resume duration (driven by the device VIP), default 1ms (FAQ 2.3.7, relevant only for remote-wakeup-from-DUT scenarios); Tdrst = host protocol/bus-reset drive duration, default 10ms (FAQ 2.3.8); sync-length overrides cfg.dev_cfg.usb_20_hs_sync_length_min=30 / usb_20_fs_sync_length_min=4 / usb_20_ls_sync_length_min=4 (FAQ 2.3.9, set on dev_cfg -- applies when VIP itself models a device). PHYSICAL/SIGNALING gotchas (FAQ Sec 2.3): DP/DM signal model uses wired-or (wor) with 9-state logic: HS drive strength=supply, FS/LS drive strength=strong, pull-down=weak, pull-up=pull (FAQ 2.3.2, lines 1143-1163) -- EXPLICIT WARNING that DUT/testbench PHY modeling must match this criteria or 'simulation anomalies are reported'; override via SVT_USB_DRIVE_STRENGTH_USER_DEFINED_{PULLDOWN0,PULLDOWN1,PULLUP0,PULLUP1,HS_TERMINATION0,HS_TERMINATION1} defines if needed (FAQ 2.3.6). Default VIP expects exactly 8 EOP bits and reports UVM_ERROR if DUT sends more (spec-legal for DUT to do so) -- fix with compile define +define+SVT_USB_20_USER_MAX_HS_EOP_LENGTH=9 (FAQ 2.3.5 and 2.3.10, same macro answers both FAQ entries). COMMON FATAL: 'UVM_FATAL remote_cfg specified with usb_20_signal_interface = UTMI_IF but usb_20_if not provided with the config db or remote_cfg' -- fix is a missing uvm_config_db#(svt_usb_if)::set(this,'host_agent','usb_20_if',this.host_usb_if) virtual-interface bind (FAQ 2.3.3, lines 1164-1172). ALIGNED-TRANSFER TERMINATION SEMANTICS (UVM guide Sec 6.4.2.1, lines 5341-5401, Host-role table -- this project's operative table since VIP=Host): with endpoint config allow_aligned_transfers_without_zero_length=0 (default) and an aligned payload, if the transfer object's aligned_transfer_with_zero_length disagrees with the endpoint config, VIP reports an 'endpoint configuration and transfer attributes are inconsistent' error but still executes using the ENDPOINT CONFIG's behavior, not the transfer's requested behavior -- a silent-override footgun worth checking when debugging unexpected zero-length-packet (or missing-ZLP) behavior on bulk/ control transfers to the Device DUT. NOTE: Sec 6.4.2.2's Device-role table (Table 6-18, line 5404) has a caption copy-paste bug reading 'describes VIP behavior when acting as a host' -- treat the table CONTENT (not the caption) as authoritative for Device-role behavior. SEQUENCE NAMING for USB2.0-applicable built-in error scenarios uses infix 20_hs_fs_30_na (i.e. 'not applicable' to SS) -- see the sequence-library-organization memory record for the full list; only these (not *_30_ss_*) apply to a 2.0-only device-mode DUT. DEBUG: VIP's own USB2.0 link-state logs are greppable by 'L20_DEV_A_SM' (Host/A-device role, this project's VIP) vs 'L20_DEV_B_SM' (Device/B-device role) (FAQ 2.2.3); +vip_verbosity=svt_usb_link_20_timer:debug isolates USB2.0 timer logging specifically (FAQ 1.16). COMPILE ESSENTIALS (GS guide Sec 2.2, lines 528-585): +define+SVT_UVM_TECHNOLOGY, +define+UVM_PACKER_MAX_BYTES=24000 (or higher -- must be set to the MAX required across all VIP titles compiled together), +define+UVM_DISABLE_AUTO_ITEM_RECORDING, +define+SYNOPSYS_SV; all VIP files must compile with timescale 1ps/1ps (silent mistiming bug risk otherwise, line 207-209); in UVM mode the top-level svt_usb_if interface MUST come from svt_usb_if.uvm.svi (not svt_usb_if.svi) to get the unparameterized interface variant (UVM guide Sec 4.2.4, lines 2214-2218).
